q: Is this dashboard connected to live customer data?
a: No. All data in this dashboard is synthetic. It is generated by generate_synthetic_data.py (seeded and reproducible), scored by the trained model and stored in a local SQLite database. The Source & Methodology page describes a proposed production lineage; it does not assert that those integrations already exist.

q: How is RFM calculated and sourced?
a: Recency is days since the latest qualifying product activity, Frequency is distinct active days in the trailing 30 days, and Monetary is Finance-approved account ARR. Each dimension is scored 1–5 within a governed cohort; Recency is reversed so 5 is best. Product telemetry is the primary source for R and F, while contract and billing data reconciled to the Finance revenue mart is the source for M. Values shown here are synthetic.

q: What does the Customer Health Score represent?
a: It is a 0–100 indicator of renewal health built from behavioral, engagement, commercial and customer-feedback signals. In this build it is 100 minus the churn model's risk score (Random Forest, 43 model signals), so 'Critical' health corresponds to the highest churn risk. A production definition should be a calibrated prediction tied to a defined renewal horizon and model version.

This build uses Excellent 80–100, Good 60–79, Fair 40–59, Poor 20–39 and Critical 0–19. “At risk” means a score below 60. Threshold changes should be versioned and approved because they change counts and trends.

q: How often should the dashboard refresh?
a: The proposed health-score refresh is weekly. CRM, renewal, owner and alert data may refresh daily or near real time, while NRR and churn should follow the Finance monthly-close schedule. Each page should show both the last successful refresh and the data-through date.

q: Why might dashboard totals differ from CRM or Finance reports?
a: Common causes include different as-of dates, account hierarchy rules, product mappings, renewal grain, currency conversion, segment changes, excluded test/internal accounts and monthly-close timing. Reconcile against governed control totals before publishing.

q: How are churn rate and NRR different?
a: Churn rate measures recurring revenue lost from customers that fully churn. NRR follows an opening revenue cohort and includes expansion, contraction and churn, but excludes new-logo revenue after the cohort starts.

q: How are churn and adoption driver impacts calculated?
a: In production, driver impacts should come from account-level model explanations aggregated for the selected cohort. A negative contribution lowers the score; a positive contribution raises it. These are model associations, not causal proof.

q: Can one account appear in multiple product totals or recommended actions?
a: Yes. A multi-product customer may be counted once in each relevant product row, so product totals can exceed the unique portfolio total. An account may also qualify for multiple actions unless a documented prioritization and deduplication rule is applied.

Product, region, segment and renewal-horizon filters should apply consistently to numerator, denominator, charts and tables. In this build the product, region, segment, risk, owner-coverage and renewal-horizon filters are applied server-side to every Action Center page; production behavior should still be validated with test cases.

q: What happens when an account has missing or stale data?
a: It should be marked Unknown or Unscored, with data-quality and freshness flags. Missing values should not be converted to zero because that can falsely lower health. Score coverage should be visible alongside portfolio averages.

q: How should alerts and recommended actions be used?
a: They are prioritization aids for owner review, not automated decisions. Owners should inspect the underlying evidence, contact history and business context before acting. Marking an alert reviewed does not remove the underlying risk.

q: Can dashboard data be exported or shared externally?
a: Exports from this build contain synthetic records only. For production, exports should respect row-level access, data classification, retention and approved sharing policies. External sharing should require a separate review and aggregation or de-identification where needed.

q: Who should approve the production methodology?
a: Recommended approvers are Customer Success Operations for operating definitions, Data Engineering for lineage and quality, Finance for ARR/NRR/churn, Product Analytics for telemetry, Support Operations for case metrics, and Privacy/Security for access and retention.
